old_problem: The historical review correctly guarded against wrong-account rename and collisions but incorrectly treated selector, encoding and collision rules as vendor-defined. IPMI standard App 45h indexes one six-bit User ID and writes an exact sixteen-byte ASCII name; App 46h returns those sixteen bytes. The standard also reserves User ID 1 for the null name, identifies fixed-name slots and explicitly assigns duplicate-name prevention to configuration software. Project inputs are limited to a dedicated configurable identity, unique temporary name, protected existing credential and audit/recovery policy.
disposition_reason: Select one enabled, disposable, non-production User ID above the fixed-name range, with no active session and an independent Administrator recovery identity. Enumerate and hash all configured names, approve a unique non-sensitive 1-15-character ASCII temporary name, encode it as NUL-terminated/zero-padded sixteen bytes, write it once with App 45h, read it exactly with App 46h, authenticate one new least-privilege session under the new name using the unchanged protected credential, correlate its audit record, close it, restore the original sixteen name bytes, and verify original login plus unchanged access/password/other-user state. User 1, fixed names, duplicate names, password/privilege/enable mutations, bulk rename, log clearing and automatic retry are excluded.
decision_basis: Master XLSX rows 1025-1028, exact same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT second review, tests_gpt_merged, selection manifest and historical V3.1 record were directly read. The exact code is unique. Formal queue sequence 63 was independently verified as row 1028 / variant a5b2d7bd6457752c.

IPMI v2.0 section 22.28 defines App NetFn 06h command 45h with request byte 1 equal to nonzero six-bit User ID and bytes 2-17 equal to an ASCII username of at most sixteen bytes. A shorter name is NUL-terminated and zero-padded; App 46h returns the exact sixteen-byte stored field.

User ID 1 is permanently the null username and cannot be configured. Get User Access reports the count of fixed-name IDs, which occupy sequential IDs beginning at 1; the test target must therefore be greater than that count and within the supported maximum.

The BMC is permitted to accept duplicate usernames and resolves login by the first enabled matching entry. The standard makes collision prevention the configuration tool's responsibility, so the runner must compare the full configured-name set before the write and refuse case-sensitive byte duplicates; no collision test is performed on the BMC.

The command changes only name storage. Password, enabled status, per-channel access and privilege are separate App 47h/43h commands and must be proven unchanged rather than rewritten or rotated in this case.

A successful 45h completion plus 46h readback proves storage, while a fresh session under the new name proves the login lookup actually resolves the intended User ID. Active sessions are excluded before the rename so the test does not rely on unspecified behavior for already authenticated sessions.

Audit text formatting is OEM/Project-specific, but the required evidence can be parameterized as an owner-approved correlation of BMC, User ID, temporary name and session time/token. Missing audit format does not change standard name semantics; it makes execution NOT READY until the Project fixture is supplied.

ED-02/ED-03/ED-13 allow an exact standard BMC contract without OEM guesses; ED-15 governs authoritative unsupported N/A; ED-18/ED-30 require authorization and identity isolation; ED-19 preserves audit evidence; ED-28 requires recovery; ED-33 through ED-38 govern package readiness, confirmation, cleanup, non-retry and engineer verdict separation.

test_case.test_name: IPMI Set User Name (App 06h/45h) unique dedicated identity rename and exact restore
test_case.purpose: Rename exactly one configurable dedicated BMC test User ID to an approved unique temporary ASCII name, prove byte-exact storage, new-name login and audit correlation without changing credentials/access, then restore the original name and prove the original identity works again.
required_package: Approved BMC/firmware and exact management channel, App 43h/44h/45h/46h/47h capability, plus independent Administrator control/recovery identity

Enabled dedicated non-production User ID in 02h..3Fh that is greater than the Get User Access fixed-name count, is not User 1/root/admin/recovery/shared, has no active session and has a known original printable nonempty name

Protected unchanged credential for the dedicated identity and immutable baselines for its sixteen name bytes, username-to-User-ID mapping, enable/access/privilege state, password-size tag if available, active sessions and all-user name-byte hashes

Owner-approved temporary name of 1-15 characters from a conservative printable ASCII fixture, encoded as bytes and proven byte-unique across every configured slot; no sensitive data or production-like name

Validated secret-safe App 45h/46h runner or upstream-equivalent `user set name` implementation with exact sixteen-byte encoding, zero automatic retries, completion/readback comparison and exact original-byte restore
Project audit-correlation fixture and immediate security confirmation binding BMC, User ID, old/new byte hashes, channel, session token, restore and recovery
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED IDENTITY-CONFIGURATION PROCEDURE; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Preserve audit/SEL and do not clear logs. Through the independent Administrator path, read maximum/fixed User ID counts and every configured App 46h name; select one enabled dedicated TEST_USER_ID greater than the fixed-name count, prove no active session, capture its original sixteen bytes plus App 44h/access/privilege/enable and credential metadata hashes. Encode approved TEMP_NAME as 1-15 printable ASCII bytes followed by 00h and zero padding to exactly sixteen bytes; reject any byte-for-byte collision with every configured name and display target/name hashes for immediate approval. Send exactly once App 06h/45h [TEST_USER_ID, TEMP_NAME_16], require completion 00h, then App 46h must return TEMP_NAME_16 exactly while all other names and App 44h state remain unchanged. Using secret-safe input and the unchanged credential, establish one fresh least-privilege session by TEMP_NAME, run only Get Device ID, correlate the audit/session entry to TEST_USER_ID/TEMP_NAME, and close it. In a finally path send exactly once App 45h [TEST_USER_ID, ORIGINAL_NAME_16], require 00h and exact 46h readback; establish one original-name Get Device ID session and close it, then verify all names/access/enable/privilege/credential/session/audit baselines. Never target User 1/fixed/production/recovery identities, use a duplicate or 16-byte unterminated test name, write password/access/enable fields, rename in bulk, expose credentials, clear logs or automatically retry.
test_case.expected_result: The exact configurable test User ID is selected and TEMP_NAME is byte-unique. The single 45h rename returns 00h; 46h returns exactly the approved NUL-terminated/zero-padded sixteen bytes, every other name and all enable/access/privilege/credential fields remain unchanged, and a new session using TEMP_NAME plus the unchanged credential performs Get Device ID and closes with correct audit correlation. The single restore returns 00h; 46h returns the exact original sixteen bytes, original-name login works, no temporary name remains, and other users/sessions/audit health are unchanged. Wrong ID, fixed/User1 target, duplicate, encoding mismatch, generic error, ambiguous timeout, unexpected account/session/audit drift or failed restore is FAIL/NOT READY without retry; authoritative absence of a configurable disposable user slot permits N/A.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact Source Key/variant, configurable dedicated User ID above fixed-name count, immutable all-user/name/access baseline, approved byte-unique 1-15 ASCII TEMP_NAME, one exact 45h write, 00h completion, exact 46h bytes, successful new-name least-privilege read and audit correlation, one exact original-byte restore, successful original-name read and unchanged credential/access/enable/other-user state. A read-only Get User Name, UI alias, User1/fixed/production target, duplicate/case-normalized assumption, sixteen-byte test name without terminator, only success code without raw readback, password or access mutation, retry, unrelated session closure, log clearing or incomplete identity cleanup cannot pass. Missing dedicated identity/credential/audit fixture/recovery is NOT READY rather than Pending review.
safety_gate: Use only an enabled disposable test User ID whose value is above the fixed-name count and which has no active session. Exclude User 1/null, fixed-name, production, shared and all control/recovery identities.

Enumerate configured names read-only and compare exact sixteen-byte values before writing. The BMC may allow duplicates, so the runner—not the BMC—must reject collisions and abort on ambiguous/case-normalized Project naming rules.
Use a non-sensitive 1-15-character conservative ASCII TEMP_NAME with explicit NUL and zero padding. Record only approved names or hashes; never embed credentials or asset secrets in the name.
Do not change password, enabled status, callback/link/IPMI access, privilege or session limit. Use protected secret input only for the two bounded login checks and never disclose it in argv/logs.
Preserve audit/security logs and close only sessions created by this test. No automatic retry: after timeout, read the exact User ID through 46h before deciding whether the one restore is needed.

Stop on wrong ID/name, collision, login resolution mismatch, audit attribution failure, access/credential drift or uncertain restore; recover only through the independent Administrator path using ORIGINAL_NAME_16.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant; BMC/firmware/channel; maximum and fixed-name counts; dedicated User ID ownership/non-production/no-active-session proof
Security approval, runner version/hash, TEMP_NAME policy and all-user exact-name collision report with protected hashes
Immutable original sixteen name bytes/hash, App 44h enable/access/privilege, credential metadata hash and session/audit baseline
Redacted exact 45h request structure, 00h response and byte-exact 46h TEMP_NAME readback plus unchanged other-user digest
TEMP_NAME Get Device ID/close and owner-approved audit correlation to the same User ID without credential exposure
Single original-byte restore, exact 46h readback, original-name Get Device ID/close, no temporary identity, unchanged account/session/audit state and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: Normal recovery is one App 45h request for the same positively identified TEST_USER_ID with the immutable ORIGINAL_NAME_16, followed by byte-exact App 46h readback and an original-name login check. On timeout, do not resend the rename; query that User ID through the independent Administrator path, compare with both approved byte arrays and perform the restore once only if needed. If the wrong User ID changed or a collision appears, stop all name writes, preserve the full name-slot/audit evidence and have the security owner restore only the affected configurable slot from its baseline. Revoke the dedicated credential only if it was exposed; verify other users and sessions before closure.

source_conflict.reason: Official sections 22.28-22.29 supply selector, length, ASCII/NUL padding, fixed-slot and duplicate-name semantics. The parameterized review-layer procedure preserves real rename/login/readback/restore coverage and excludes the source's unsafe log-clear boilerplate.

project_authority: The Project security/BMC owners designate the configurable disposable User ID, approve TEMP_NAME and collision/audit policy, protect the existing credential, validate the runner and issue the verdict. They may approve N/A only with authoritative evidence that no configurable disposable slot exists. Approval cannot target fixed/production/recovery identities, allow duplicate/ambiguous names, alter password/access/enable state, merge adjacent command coverage, retry automatically, clear logs or accept incomplete restoration.
